record.title: SWE-Proof reports that machine-checkable specifications improve issue resolution, while specification faithfulness limits autonomous gains
record.summary: The v2 SWE-Proof paper builds a 500-issue benchmark from SWE-bench Verified and a Python subset of SWE-bench Pro, pairing each issue with a formal specification, a verifying implementation, and a ground-truth patch. On SWE-bench Verified, the authors report that a correctly supplied specification raised resolution from an 85% unaided baseline to about 95%, while adding verification to an end-to-end agent that writes its own specification did not improve its roughly 85% baseline. In a separate specification-synthesis test, only 56% of model-written specifications passed the paper’s five-property audit; incomplete behavioral coverage (faithfulness) was the main failure. The results are author-reported. Their guarantee depends on audited axioms and faithful refinement from verified code to the executed patch, and the audit panel itself uses language models.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports a 500-issue benchmark covering SWE-bench Verified and a Python fragment of SWE-bench Pro, with formal specifications, verifying implementations, ground-truth patches and recorded gate outcomes.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On SWE-bench Verified, the authors report that a correct supplied specification increases issue resolution from about 85% unaided to about 95%; verification catches defects that the held-out tests miss.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: When the agent must synthesize its own specification, end-to-end resolution shows no gain over the unaided baseline; only 56% of synthesized specifications pass the paper’s five-property audit, with faithfulness the main failure.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper states that its verify-implies-resolve guarantee depends on audited axiom soundness and fidelity of refinement from the verified implementation to the executed patch; specification audits are evidence from a language-model panel, not a mathematical proof of the full pipeline.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent recomputation of the benchmark outcomes, repeated-run variation or verification-vs-test comparison has been performed.
The authors’ axiom-soundness and refinement-fidelity evidence, including language-model audit panels, has not been independently red-teamed.
Transfer to other programming languages, repositories, issue distributions and verification backends is not established by the headline result.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported benchmark results hold in this formal-methods regime, supplying a faithful machine-checkable specification can materially raise issue-resolution success and expose a class of defects hidden by tests. The work changes evaluation and verification design for repository agents, but self-generated specification synthesis remains weak and the result is not a general proof of autonomous software correctness.
limitations: The guarantee is conditional on the soundness of axioms and fidelity of the refinement from verified implementation to executed patch.
The specification audit is a calibrated language-model panel; its verdicts are evidence, not proof.

Model-generated specifications and artifacts remain difficult to synthesize faithfully: only 56% of specifications in the cited synthesis setting passed the five-property audit, with faithfulness the dominant failure.
A few instances use manual modeling or relax a secondary no-leakage property, limiting their evidential strength.
All outcome, benchmark and audit results are author-reported; the research desk has not independently rerun the pipeline or inspected bundle artifacts.

The central comparison is conditional on supplied formal specifications and specific SWE-bench tasks; it does not establish autonomous formal verification across arbitrary repositories or software properties.

The results are author-reported. Their guarantee depends on audited axioms and faithful refinement from verified code to the executed patch, and the audit panel itself uses language models.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report that hidden tests miss about one quarter of defects caught by verification, and that a correct supplied formal specification raises SWE-bench Verified resolution from an approximately 85% unaided baseline to approximately 95%. End-to-end agents writing their own specifications do not improve the baseline; the specification-synthesis setting reports 56% of specifications passing the five-property audit.
technical.compute_or_cost: 500 issues are benchmarked; specifications use several verification backends. Reconstructing the entire corpus is reported as expensive; per-instance artifacts and recorded gate outcomes are intended to support rechecking.
technical.demonstrated_result: The v2 arXiv paper describes its 500-instance benchmark, verification pipeline, evaluation settings, audit procedures, reported outcomes and limitations. No independent rerun of the benchmark or inspection of the released proof bundles has been completed; all performance and trustworthiness results remain author-reported.
technical.implementation_status: Authors report a pipeline that checks proof obligations, execution/refinement equivalence, axioms, specification soundness/completeness/faithfulness, and leakage. Each instance includes a proof bundle and gate outcomes in the announced release.
technical.mechanism: Benchproofer constructs formal specifications, axiomatizes unchanged repository behavior, and admits benchmark instances only after mechanical checks and adversarial language-model audits. A candidate patch must refine an implementation that verifies against the specification.
technical.novelty: Applies machine-checked formal specifications to real repository issues with a paired pre-fix implementation, reference patch and audited proof bundle, while measuring the gap between supplied and self-synthesized specifications.
technical.regime: Repository issue resolution on SWE-bench Verified (500 issues) and the Python fragment of SWE-bench Pro. Evaluated models/verifiers and budgets vary by formal backend; headline 85-to-95 comparison is on SWE-bench Verified.
technical.reproducibility: Paper says the construction pipeline and all instance artifacts will be released. The release has not been independently downloaded or audited.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within-paper SWE-bench Verified comparisons include an unaided baseline, an end-to-end setting where the agent writes a specification and patch, and a verified-from-spec setting where the specification is supplied. Appendix reports repeated runs for major settings.

brief.title: SWE-Proof reports that machine-checkable specifications improve issue resolution, while specification faithfulness limits autonomous gains
brief.why_it_matters: The paper separates proof checking from the harder task of expressing the intended behavior faithfully. Its reported gap suggests formal verification can catch defects missed by tests when the specification is sound, while an agent that writes its own incomplete specification can gain little. This is consequential for software-agent evaluation and tool design, but does not show that general coding agents can autonomously produce correct proofs or specifications in ordinary repositories.
